newsitem.title: USA: Senate Finance chair says pleased with IRS nominee.
newsitem.headline: Senate Finance chair says pleased with IRS nominee.

text.p: The chairman of the Senate committee that will take up the nomination of the new chief for the Internal Revenue Service said Wednesday he was "pleased" with President Clinton's expected nominee.
Clinton plans to name Charles Rossotti, head of American Management Systems, of Fairfax, Virginia, as new head of the IRS, administration officials have said.
"I am pleased that the President has chosen someone with a distinguished management background as Mr. Rossotti appears to have," Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth said.
"The IRS is in great need of a leader who has significant management experience," the Delaware Republican said. The committee has not yet received the nomination.
IRS Commissioner Margaret Richardson, who assumed the top IRS post in May 1993, announced in January she was resigning to seek other career opportunities.

The IRS has been under fire in Congress over management issues and a congressionally-appointed commission is expected to recommend this month the establishment of an independent board to oversee the tax-collection agency.
